body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: 4bf94bdba24d674bfab70b13a9b3e8a496a9ed4c -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** The claim "only the display is stale; no path posts on B without being checked" is proven for the laws and routes below, and closing #1241 is right.

**What looks good**
- Both remount routes are covered, each through its own test: `SetSetupMachine` (setup) and `LoadMachine` (document), via one `Via` enum.
- The stale cached path is never regenerated. The only `GenerateOperation` is on machine A, before the switch. After the switch the tests assert op status `Ok`, then `verification_gate` is non-empty, then `post_setup` is refused.
- The refusals are asserted by name: `machine TightMill:`, the tool/rpm line (`above the machine's 1000`), `Face1: move ... the stroke is -10.000..10.000`, `tilts the tool ... states no tilting rotary`, and `a ... operation cannot run on its setup's ... machine`. Every refusal also asserts that no file was written.
- Undo (A posts again), redo (B refused again) and save/reopen (still refused) are covered for the stroke/rpm and rotary laws. Family is covered for undo only.
- Header and Gate map match the neighbouring suites; the file is 292 lines; no product code or golden changed. The decision note records the roomy-one reasoning, the options dropped and the cost of changing it.

**Post-time pinning, by law (read from `posting.rs` / `posting_mounts.rs` / `posting_family.rs`)**
| Law | Re-read at post time | Pinned by the tests |
|---|---|---|
| Travel limits | `verification_report_by` -> `mounts::machine_problems` -> `check_ops` (`posting.rs:682`) | yes, both routes, post + gate |
| Max spindle rpm | same `check_ops` clause | yes, both routes (same asserted block as travel) |
| No tilting rotary (pose) | same gate clause | yes, both routes (tilt-head -> VMC 3-axis) |
| Machine kind | `family_at_post` in `op_streams` (`posting.rs:832`) | yes, both routes (mill -> Lathe) |
| Missing 4th axis for an index/rotary move | not separately tested | no |
| Per-mount post (`post_mounts`) and per-op post (`post_per_op`) | the same `verification_report_by` (`posting_per_op.rs:136`); `post_mounts` falls through to `post_setup` for one mount | not in the PR (the PR says so) |

**Local results, merged with `origin/main` 0757563d (trial merge clean)**
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test machine_switch`: 6 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test machine_switch -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Throwaway probe, not pushed: I added a test that switches the machine through both routes with the stale path in place. `post_mounts` and `post_per_op` both refuse with `TightMill`, and per-op writes no files. So the two post paths the PR does not exercise do hold, for a single mount. A multi-mount program on mixed machines was not probed.

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
1. Display vs. gate: issue question (1) is answered "not shown stale", by design. The decision note records why: the M2.3 roomy-one law, pinned by `fixtures.rs::workholding_never_stales_a_fresh_toolpath`. "Done means" allows "or the issue records why it need not", so `Fixes #1241` is acceptable. The gate is live, and there is a visible by-name refusal at post and in the verify gate. If the maintainer wants a visible hint, the note's "generated on <machine A>" idea would be a P7 follow-up, not a reason to keep this open.
2. Optional hardening: pin `post_mounts` / `post_per_op` after a switch (my probe shows it holds), and add a 4th-axis indexing case. The family test could also cover redo and reopen.
3. The `Ok` asserts after the switch pin the roomy-one law. A later decision to stale on a machine switch will need those flipped, as the note says.
4. The tests reach the machine checks only through the gate, not `machine::check_ops` directly; fine.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
